canonical.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
canonical.sourceFilePath: 08. Sliding Window/1. Medium Problems/04. Longest Repeating Character.cpp

narrative.title: The Mural Touch-Up Painter
narrative.scenario: A restorer inspects a long mural strip of colored tiles, each already painted one uppercase-coded color, and carries k cans of touch-up paint — each can repaints one tile into any color. The studio asks for the longest solid single-color band the restorer can produce. The painter evaluates a frame by asking one question: can the minority tiles inside it all be repainted within budget?
narrative.inputFormat: A string s of uppercase English letters and an integer k, the repaint budget.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the length of the longest single-letter substring achievable with at most k replacements.
constraints: s consists of uppercase English letters

testCases.explanation: Two repaints turn either letter into the other across the whole strip.
The best band is "ABBA"-shaped: one repaint makes it four identical letters.

starterCode.python:
def character_replacement(s: str, k: int) -> int:
    count = {}          # letter -> frequency in window
    start = top = best = 0   # top = highest single-letter frequency seen
    for i, ch in enumerate(s):
        count[ch] = count.get(ch, 0) + 1
        top = max(top, count[ch])
        while (i - start + 1) - top > k:
            count[s[start]] -= 1
            start += 1
        best = max(best, i - start + 1)
    return best

hintLevels: Level 1: A window is upgradeable when (length - most frequent letter count) fits in k repaints.
Level 2: Track the dominant letter's frequency; the frame is valid while the minorities stay within budget.
Level 3: The dominant frequency may go stale after evictions, but the answer window only ever grows — staleness never overestimates.
